newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-"THE GREAT ONE" STILL HAS HIS MAGIC.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-"THE GREAT ONE" STILL HAS HIS MAGIC.

text.p: Wayne Gretzky came to New York Rangers this year with many believing his magic was gone, or at least fading.

Neither his lifelong dominance of the sport nor his reunion with former Edmonton Oiler teammate Mark Messier could contain the doubts: He was 36 years old now, had played for 19 years and had lost a step; he rarely captured a game the way he used to; the goals were not pouring out of him anymore.
His leadership, his playmaking skills and assists were all he had left to give a team, his critics carped.

Gretzky seized Game Two of the National Hockey League Eastern Conference finals -- and the hearts of Rangers fans -- on Sunday with three straight goals to beat the Philadelphia Flyers 5-4 and tie the series at one game apiece.

In the first period, with the game tied 1-1, Gretzky flew with the puck across the mouth of the goal past Flyers goaltender Garth Snow. And then, going against the grain of play, he sneaked a backward shot into the corner of the net.
Two minutes later, Gretzky scored with one of his signature plays, a shot from behind the net that caromed of the skate of an opposing player.
In the second period, the league's all-time leading scorer pumped a slapshot past Snow, who was replaced by Ron Hextall later in the period after allowing a fifth Rangers score.
Gretzky's hat trick raised to 121 his all-time playoff goals.
Compare the Great One -- a nickname that will ultimately fail to live up to his career -- to the playoff goal total of other great ones.
Gordie Howe of the Detroit Red Wings had 68. Maurice "Rocket" Richard, one of the most legendary of the fabled Montreal Canadiens, had 82. Richard's total was once thought unsurpassable.
Who is Gretzky's closest playoff-goal rival now?

It's his linemate, Messier, the Rangers captain. Messier, playing Gretzky's customary center's position on the line, found the back of the net once himself on Sunday to raise his playoff goal total to 109.
"I played 19 years in the NHL as a centre but playing with Messier makes it a lot easier," Gretzy said after the game. "I'm no Gordie Howe out there."
This is true. Numbers do not lie.
Gretzky was demure about his performance. "It was my night for the puck to go in. I just got a little lucky," he said sheepishly.
Messier sees it differently: "Wayne has been lucky for 20 years."
